newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold under pressure, may erode further.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold under pressure, may erode further.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold was vulnerable to further tests of the downside and may target recent lows around $320 and a support line at $318, analysts said.
Silver was having trouble overcoming resistance at $4.58/$4.60 and was seen moving sideways, they added.
GOLD -
A weak performance on Monday could set the scene for more probes of support.
"With the RSI dipping down in confirmation, look to continued tests of the downside," analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
The 14-day RSI was at 43 at Monday's close, which provides plenty of scope on the downside before oversold levels are hit around 30.
Recent lows just above $320 should provide the first line of attack for the bears, at Monday's $320.80 and the August 8 low of $320.40.

Technical analyst Karen Jones said: "We've got a support line which connects the recent lows that we've seen in July and August. This comes in today at $318, and I suspect that's where we're going today."
At 0735 GMT spot gold was quoted at $321.50/321.90, up 40 cents from Monday's New York close.
SILVER -

After inching higher for the past few weeks, the market has been turned back at resistance around $4.57 and $4.58, the highs of Monday and Friday respectively. This also coincides with the high of July 4.

"We're seeing silver struggle to overcome this area...I think it's likely to hold sideways here in the near term," said Jones, adding that prices could come down to test last week's lows around $4.38/$4.39.
Support here would be reinforced by the 30-day moving average at $4.37.
Added support for silver and more pressure on gold came from a soggy gold-silver ratio, Jones said.
The ratio was around 71.28 early on Tuesday morning.
It was likely to test 69.70, a break of which would bring it down to 68.00, Jones added.
At 0735 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.51/4.53, down one cent from Monday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was still in a downtrend since topping at $465 on August 5 and could see more weakness, with Monday's low at $413 the first floor.
Further support was seen around $408, which was the short-term target, and a downtrend line would offer resistance on Tuesday at $423, Jones said.
Recent highs around $430 would be the next resistance levels, other analysts said.
At 0735 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $416.00/419.00, up $1.00 from Monday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
